_comment: Three flat-severity rounds that split into three different invariant signatures, each on a different file, and none of them naming what the shared module exports. No single class can substantiate the seam, but the files collectively do — two or more flagged files importing it is the same evidence the class-level rule uses. This is the signature drift the rollup exists to catch, so it must gate.

findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate the row after the await**

The row is read before the await and written after it, so a concurrent archive wins the race and nothing revalidates it in between.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat an absent record as empty**

When the record is missing this returns undefined and the caller reads a null field; return an empty list.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Roll back the stamp when the write throws**

The stamp is persisted first and never rolled back on failure, so the next caller overwrites it.
